title: Jasper Discord Q&A — GEX vs gamma ladder disambiguation
description:
Principal-sourced Discord Q&A. Freddy Sarmiento asks Jasper about a confusion in the GEX profile, Jasper answers directly with the clearest disambiguation of the two ladders we have:

> the "gex" profile is netted out calls vs puts, ignoring long/short.
> the purple/cyan ladder "gamma" is long/short contracts, ignoring call/put
> call/put gex -> measure of directional (up/down) convexity
> long/short gamma -> measure of momentum/reversion (continuation or fade)

This is the operational labeling that ties the two ladders to two different trading questions. Existing canonical/gex_profile.md and canonical/convexity_ladder.md each document one axis; this Q&A is what makes the two axes legible as a system.

## Acceptance Criteria
- New canonical/principal_discord.md (parallel to community/discord_quotes.md, but for principal-tier voices: Jasper "Jass", John Kirby)
- Q&A archived verbatim with date, channel, both speakers tagged
- Cross-references added from gex_profile.md and convexity_ladder.md
- Disambiguation table extracted as a reusable operational handle

title: Three-stream corpus: Schwab + GexBot + Databento OPRA
description:
## Goal

Stand up per-day, append-only ledger of three independent market data streams so we can read the late-day 0DTE gamma/charm footprints across many sessions. Building the corpus is the prerequisite for any model-mastery work — without a multi-day record, we cannot validate (or falsify) GexBot's classification against raw OPRA tape.

## Streams

1. **Schwab session record** — spot SPX + /ES quotes, 0DTE ATM chain (±10 strikes) snapshot, ATM straddle, ATM IV. 5-min cadence during cash hours (8:30-15:00 CT). Free (entitlement via brokerage).

2. **GexBot State** — `/SPX/state/{gamma,vanna,charm,delta}_zero` plus `/SPX/classic/gex_zero/majors` (the only majors endpoint that works for our tier per the st-rks probe). 5-min cadence. Flat $150/mo.

3. **Databento OPRA option ticks** — all SPXW (incl 0DTE) trades for the late-day window (13:00-15:00 CT initially). Historical batch pull, T+1, dataset=`OPRA.PILLAR`, schema=`trades`, symbols=["SPXW.OPT"], stype_in=`parent`. ~$6-8 per session per get_cost probe (verified entitled 2026-05-22).

## Storage

Per-day directory `data/corpus/YYYY-MM-DD/`:
- `schwab.jsonl` — append, one row per intraday cycle
- `gexbot.jsonl` — append, one row per intraday cycle, all 5 endpoint responses bundled
- `databento_opra.jsonl` — written once per day by T+1 batch
- `manifest.json` — what was collected, when, errors

JSONL = append-only, easy to inspect with jq, cheap incremental reads. `data/corpus/` gitignored (corpus grows large).

## Scripts

- `scripts/corpus_pull_schwab.py` — one cycle, idempotent, writes one JSONL line
- `scripts/corpus_pull_gexbot.py` — one cycle, all 5 endpoints, writes one line
- `scripts/corpus_pull_databento.py` — batch pull for a given date (run T+1)
- `scripts/corpus_poll.py` — orchestrator: runs Schwab + GexBot together; loop with --max-runs / --interval

## Acceptance Criteria

- All four scripts compile and run end-to-end smoke against live APIs
- One Schwab cycle, one GexBot cycle, and one Databento batch (yesterday 2026-05-21 SPXW late-day) all produce well-formed JSONL with timestamps and full provenance
- Data field provenance: every value cites its source endpoint and the response timestamp it came from
- `data/corpus/` is gitignored
- No interpretive labels (no "regime", no "pinning") in the raw stream — those are derivations for later
- ~/.schwab_gate_key check honored for the Schwab stream
- Databento cost stays in the $6-8/session range for the chosen window

## Why P1

Steve flagged 2026-05-22 that the framework can't progress without a corpus. Every "vet read" attempt I've made has been ungrounded interpretive content because I don't have multi-day pattern data to anchor on. The corpus IS the substrate. Until it exists, my opinions on a given day's late-day move aren't reliably worth more than noise. Parent bead: st-rks (which scoped Layer 4 measurement; this expands and supersedes that layer's design).
close_reason:
Corpus stood up end-to-end in commit e1913b2. All three streams landed:

(1) Schwab + GexBot polling (intraday): one-cycle scripts plus orchestrator. Verified 2026-05-22 pre-open: 1 Schwab row (SPX 7445.72, ATM K 7445), 1 GexBot row (5 endpoints bundled, gamma_zero spot 7445.29, mpos 7450 / mneg 7445 / mLg 7439.80 / mSg 7449.68). Both clean, no errors.

(2) Databento OPRA batch (T+2): historical pull verified on 2026-05-18 13:00-13:05 CT validation window — 21,198 SPXW ticks with full OSI symbology (e.g., SPXW  260518P07395000) at $0.50.

Two operational findings logged in commit:
- Databento OPRA historical embargo: data after [yesterday market open] requires Live license. Effective limit: T+2 batch from today, T+1 if pulled before market open. Documented; not blocking for corpus purposes (learning, not trading intraday).
- Symbology requires to_df() not raw iteration. First-attempt pull 2026-05-20 (349k ticks, $4.37) had null symbols; bug caught and corrected on validation pull. 5/20 file retained on disk with intact prices/sizes/instrument_ids/timestamps but per-strike attribution would need a symbology backfill if revived.

Total spend: ~$5 ($4.37 broken first pull + $0.50 validation pull on the corrected code). Going-forward cadence: ~$5-8 per session at the 2-hour late-day window.

AC met: (a) all 4 scripts compile + run end-to-end smoke against live APIs ✓, (b) JSONL well-formed with full provenance ✓, (c) data/corpus/ gitignored via top-level data/ ✓, (d) no interpretive labels (regime, pinning) in raw stream ✓, (e) Schwab gate honored ✓, (f) Databento spend in target range ✓.

Next step for the corpus is to actually run it: corpus_poll.py on a 5-min cron during cash hours (8:30-15:00 CT) plus corpus_pull_databento.py invoked T+2 each morning for the prior session's late-day window. Pattern study comes after ~5-10 days accumulate.

title: Canonical-vs-measured comparison framework
description:
## Goal

Build the third box in the canonical/community/measured architecture: pure-function comparators that take a corpus row plus a canonical assertion and emit pass / fail / divergence outputs. This is the box that makes the canonical/measured separation operationally useful — without it, the canonical docs are just shelf decoration.

## Architecture context

The directory layout (per docs/gexbot/README.md) separates:
- **Canonical** (docs/{vendor}/canonical/) — verbatim vendor-published truth, immutable
- **Community** (docs/{vendor}/community/) — practitioner interpretations
- **Measured** (data/corpus/) — what we actually observed cycle-by-cycle

This bead adds the comparison layer.

## What the framework does

Given:
- A canonical assertion (e.g. "customer-long strikes act as walls — price gravitates toward them and stalls in declining-vol environments")
- A corpus row or window (gexbot.jsonl + schwab.jsonl + databento_opra.jsonl for one timestamp or window)

Emit:
- **PASS** — measurement supports the canonical claim (price did stall at the predicted strike under the predicted regime)
- **FAIL** — measurement contradicts the canonical claim (price blew through the predicted wall)
- **DIVERGENCE** — outcome doesn't fit either, often because a modifying canonical condition was not satisfied (e.g. "this was a rising-vol session and the canonical text says walls are vulnerable in rising vol — outcome was a failed wall, consistent with the modifier")
- **N/A** — preconditions for the assertion didn't hold (couldn't evaluate)

## Likely module layout

```
market/corpus/
  checks/
    __init__.py
    base.py             # Assertion / Check / Result types
    options_profile.py  # Checks corresponding to canonical/options_profile.md
    runner.py           # Iterate corpus rows, evaluate all registered checks
data/corpus/YYYY-MM-DD/
  check_results.jsonl   # Output: one row per (assertion × cycle) evaluation
```

## Initial check set (from canonical/options_profile.md)

1. **Wall behavior under declining vol** — at major_long_gamma strikes, does spot stall (defined: price approaches within N pts, doesn't break by M pts within K minutes)?
2. **Accelerator behavior under declining vol** — at major_short_gamma strikes, does spot pass through (define passes-through threshold)?
3. **Wall vulnerability under rising vol** — does the wall pass-through rate go up when ATM IV trajectory across cycles is rising?
4. **Short-side inversion under rising vol** — do major_short_gamma strikes start behaving more like walls in rising-vol sessions?

Each check needs explicit threshold definitions, regime detection logic (IV trajectory from Schwab chain), and falsification conditions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `market/corpus/checks/` package exists with `base.py` types
- At least one canonical assertion (the wall-under-declining-vol claim) implemented end-to-end
- Runner produces `check_results.jsonl` for one trading day of corpus data
- Output is structured (assertion ID, cycle ts, result, evidence fields) — readable with jq
- Each check declares its preconditions and falsification conditions in code, not just prose

## Non-goals

- Beautiful dashboards (CLI / JSONL output is enough)
- Auto-flipping canonical claims based on results (humans interpret)
- Multi-vendor checks (start with GexBot; pattern generalizes later)

## Why P2

Stand the corpus up first (st-1yp ✓), then accumulate days of paired data. Only useful to write checks once we have data to run them against. ~5-10 trading days of corpus data is enough to make initial checks meaningful.

title: GexBot State integration — probe, distillation, measurement harness
description:
## Goal

One-month evaluation of GexBot State ($150) as a vanna/charm intelligence layer for the late-day fly strategy. Build a thin, focused integration that emits a daily decision-grade signal Steve can act on without needing to read GEX ladders himself, plus a measurement harness that produces an empirical day-30 renew/cancel verdict.

## Architecture

**Layer 1 — Ingest.** `market/ingest/gexbot.py` provides `make_client()` (IPv4-only httpx with bearer auth, WSL IPv6 broken on this distro) and `fetch_state()`. API spec saved at `docs/gexbot/gexbot.spec3.yaml` (upstream: github.com/nfa-llc/gexbot-openapi master, v2.2.0). Base URL: `https://api.gex.bot/v2`. Auth: `Authorization: Bearer gexbot_custom_<key>`. Key in `.env` as `GEXBOT_API_KEY`. Rate limit 1 req/sec/metric per spec.

**Layer 2 — Distill.** `market/ingest/gexbot.py:distill()` consumes a state-tier response and emits a 4-tuple:
- `center_strike: int` — best EOD center, derived from `major_positive`/`major_negative` proximity to spot
- `regime: 'pinning' | 'trending' | 'unclear'` — derived from range width (V1 thresholds: <50 pinning, >100 trending)
- `confidence: 'low' | 'med' | 'high'` — derived from edge distance + zero-gamma transition risk
- `reason: str` — one plain-English sentence

V1 thresholds are educated guesses; real calibration comes after Layer 4 has data.

**Layer 3 — Pair with tape read.** TODO. Daily emission gets logged alongside Steve's manual tape-read center call. Format mirrors `gex_series.py` JSONL — one line per emission with timestamp, GexBot distillation, Steve's read, and (after EOD) the actual print.

**Layer 4 — Measure.** TODO. `data/gexbot_calibration/SPX_YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl`. After ~20 trading days, two numbers: (a) GexBot agent's center hit-rate within 5pts of EOD print, (b) Steve's tape-read hit-rate. Drives renew/cancel decision.

## Endpoints in scope (per spec; corrected after probe)

**Classic tier (table-stakes, paid by Steve's State sub):**
- `/SPX/classic/gex_zero` — 0DTE GEX (basic_response with `zero_gamma`, `major_pos_vol`/`major_pos_oi`, `major_neg_vol`/`major_neg_oi`, `strikes`)
- `/SPX/classic/gex_zero/majors` — key levels (classic-only; `/majors` does not exist for state endpoints — verified via probe 400 response)

**State tier (the differentiated value):**
- `/SPX/state/gamma_zero` — 0DTE orderflow-classified gamma. Top-level fields include `major_positive`, `major_negative`, `major_long_gamma`, `major_short_gamma`, `zero_gamma`. Strike-level data in `mini_contracts` array.
- `/SPX/state/vanna_zero` — 0DTE vanna (late-day reversal driver)
- `/SPX/state/charm_zero` — 0DTE charm (per-hour decay)

## Deliverables

1. ✅ `scripts/gexbot_probe.py` — connectivity diagnostic (LANDED commit 1643fdf)
2. ✅ `market/ingest/gexbot.py` — client + distillation module (THIS commit)
3. ✅ `scripts/gexbot_distill.py` — one-shot runner emitting the 4-tuple (THIS commit)
4. ❌ Pairing harness — Steve's manual tape-read input + post-EOD print backfill (next session)
5. ❌ Cadence runner — append-mode JSONL persistence at `data/gexbot_calibration/SPX_YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` (next session)
6. ❌ Day-30 measurement script — renew/cancel verdict numbers (after ~20 days of pairings)

## Acceptance Criteria

- ✅ Probe returns non-error JSON for /tickers + auth'd SPX endpoints
- ✅ Distillation produces all 4 fields from a real SPX state response — verified against live 2026-05-21 08:34 SPX data: spot 7404.52, center 7405, regime trending, confidence med
- ❌ JSONL persistence writes one line per invocation matching schema
- ❌ Pairing harness lets Steve log daily tape-read center + EOD print
- ❌ Measurement script consumes ~20 days and emits hit-rate verdict numbers
- ✅ Rate limiting respected (probe sleeps 1.1s between calls)

## Non-goals

- Websocket feed (REST polling is enough)
- Historical backfill via `/hist`
- Trade execution (evaluating signal quality only)
- Multi-ticker (SPX only for the eval)

## V1 threshold calibration notes

Initial thresholds are SPX/0DTE estimates, untested against outcomes:
- Range <50pts → pinning (tight 0DTE range, high gamma)
- Range >100pts → trending (wide range, low gamma anchor)
- Spot within 25% of an edge → center on that edge
- Spot within 5pts of zero_gamma → confidence drops to low (transition)

These get recalibrated once Layer 4 has 20+ days of paired outcomes.

## Authorizing context

CSO: COO-driven, see CLAUDE.md / project_coo-drives-strader-initial.md memory and feedback_make-brainstorm-decisions.md. Built off Steve's directive 2026-05-21 to absorb a one-month $150 GexBot State subscription after FlashAlpha free tier proved unusable. Day-30 renew/cancel decision is the deliverable, not the integration itself.
close_reason: Closing with supersession note. Three deliverables landed end-to-end (probe / distillation module / one-shot runner — commits 1643fdf + 41fb337). The remaining three deliverables (pairing harness / cadence runner / day-30 measurement script) were superseded by st-1yp (three-stream corpus) which expanded scope to Schwab + GexBot + Databento OPRA together rather than the original Schwab + GexBot pair. Bead st-1yp landed the cadence runner (scripts/corpus_poll.py), the structured persistence (data/corpus/YYYY-MM-DD/), and the per-day manifest. The day-30 renew/cancel measurement was promoted to its own bead st-cgb (canonical-vs-measured comparison framework, P2 deferred until corpus accumulates data). Net: original scope fully covered across the trio st-rks + st-1yp + st-cgb, with cleaner architecture than the original bead anticipated.

title: _try_quote() 400s on /ES futures — use get_quotes() not get_quote()
description:
## Symptom

`_try_quote(client, '/ES')` in scripts/gex_series.py:118 always returns None for ES futures. `client.get_quote('/ES')` returns the ES *equity* (Eversource Energy, COE) instead of the futures contract; `/ESM26` and `/ESU26` return HTTP 400.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `.venv/bin/python scripts/_debug_es_quote.py`
2. Observe: `/ESM26` and `/ESU26` both return 400 with URL `https://api.schwabapi.com/marketdata/v1//ESM26/quotes` (note double slash).
3. Observe: `/ES` returns assetMainType=EQUITY (Eversource Energy ticker ES, not the futures contract).

## Root cause

schwab-py's `get_quote(symbol)` interpolates the symbol into the URL path:

  /marketdata/v1/{symbol}/quotes

For `/ESM26` this produces `/marketdata/v1//ESM26/quotes` — double slash, 400. The library's own docstring (base.py:176-179) warns against using `get_quote()` for symbols with non-alphanumeric characters and points users to `get_quotes()` (plural), which sends the symbol as a query parameter and dodges the URL-path issue.

## Fix

1. scripts/gex_series.py:118 — `client.get_quote(symbol)` → `client.get_quotes([symbol])`. Response shape unchanged (`{symbol: {...}}`), existing payload.values() loop is correct.
2. schwab/readers/quote.py:17 — collapse the len-1 special case; always call `get_quotes`. Currently latent: any single-symbol call with `/ES` would hit the same bug.
3. Delete scripts/_debug_es_quote.py (script's own header marks it for deletion once `_try_quote` is fixed).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `scripts/gex_series.py --max-runs 1` records a non-null `spot_es` in the JSONL output when called with `--es-symbol /ESM26` (or whichever front-month ES contract is current).
- Re-running `scripts/_debug_es_quote.py` with `get_quotes` instead of `get_quote` returns a futures-shaped quote for `/ESM26` (assetMainType=FUTURE, not EQUITY).
- _debug_es_quote.py is removed after the fix verifies.
close_reason: Fix landed in commit c56961c. Both call sites (scripts/gex_series.py:_try_quote and schwab/readers/quote.py) now use get_quotes() (plural) which sends symbol as query parameter, bypassing the path-interpolation double-slash that 400'd futures lookups. Verified end-to-end: /ES, /ESM26, /ESU26 all return assetMainType=FUTURE with real prices via get_quotes (ESM26 last 7447, ESU26 last 7507, ~60pt contango premium on the September contract — sane ES term-structure shape). scripts/_debug_es_quote.py removed.

title: GEX series loop: pull chain + recompute GEX on interval, append to JSONL time-series
description:
## Goal

Long-running script that snapshots GEX on a cadence and persists each snapshot to JSONL. Bridges static GEX read → live regime / trajectory tracker.

## Scope

- scripts/gex_series.py:
  - Inserts lib/schwab-py at sys.path[0] (same pattern as gex_now.py)
  - Gate-key check
  - Loops on --interval seconds (default 60s; Schwab gammas update slowly enough)
  - Each cycle: pull bounded chain (default strike_count=30, dte=0), compute GEX, append a JSONL line, print a one-line summary
  - Configurable: --symbol, --strikes, --dte, --interval, --max-runs, --output-dir
  - Graceful shutdown on Ctrl-C: prints summary stats (cycles run, file path)
  - Date-rotated output: data/gex_series/SYMBOL_YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl

- JSONL schema per line:
  - ts (ISO US/Central)
  - symbol, spot, n_strikes
  - net_gex, net_gex_calls, net_gex_puts
  - top_wall (strike with largest positive gamma, with magnitude)
  - top_slide (strike with most negative net contribution, with magnitude)
  - regime ('SUPPRESSIVE' | 'AMPLIFYING')
  - by_strike (dict; truncated to strikes within ±50 of spot)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Script runs without OAuth prompt if token is valid and gate is set
- Each cycle appends one valid JSONL line; file readable by jq
- Console one-liner shows timestamp, spot, net_gex, top wall — visible at a glance
- --max-runs 1 produces exactly one cycle (smoke-test mode)
- Ctrl-C exits cleanly with final summary

## Out of scope (follow-up beads)

- Plotting / visualization of the series (separate)
- Wire to Databento ticks for spot updates between chain pulls (separate)
- Alert emission on regime flip or large GEX shift (separate)
- Persistence to parquet via polars (defer to when series gets long; JSONL is fine for hours-of-day)
close_reason: GEX series loop landed. scripts/gex_series.py snapshots SPX GEX on a cadence, persists to data/gex_series/SYMBOL_YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl, prints one-line console summary. Captures SPX cash + ES quote + basis per cycle so ES-chart cross-references work explicitly. Tolerates transient Schwab errors (logs and continues). Smoke-tested via --help and --max-runs 1 path (clean exit; ready for live run when Steve has the gate set).

title: Hobble local schwab-py fork: structurally remove account/order/transaction methods
description:
## Goal

Structural API gate. Currently the gate is behavioral (~/.schwab_gate_key file check). A determined or careless code path bypasses it. By physically removing account-touching methods from our local schwab-py fork, the methods literally do not exist — typos and AI mistakes get AttributeError, not real API calls.

## Scope

Methods to remove (12, all account/order/transaction surface):
- get_account, get_account_numbers, get_accounts
- get_order, cancel_order, place_order, replace_order, preview_order
- get_orders_for_account, get_orders_for_all_linked_accounts
- get_transactions, get_transaction

Methods to keep: everything market-data-only (quotes, chains, history, scanners, instruments, market hours). Also keep get_user_preferences (per Steve's call — useful for token verification).

## Steps

1. Initialize the lib/schwab-py submodule (currently empty; tracks github.com/justSteve/schwab-py)
2. pip uninstall pypi schwab-py; pip install -e the local fork
3. Strip 12 methods × 3 files (base.py, synchronous.py, asynchronous.py)
4. Strip matching test cases in tests/client_tests.py
5. Add DEFENSE NOTE header in base.py
6. Verify existing market-data scripts (gex_now.py, hello_schwab.py) still work
7. Commit + push to the fork
8. Update Strader's submodule pointer
9. Keep the ~/.schwab_gate_key as belt-and-suspenders (defense in depth)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Removed methods raise AttributeError when called from a Strader script
- Market-data calls (get_option_chain, get_quote, get_price_history) still work
- Strader pytest tests still pass (97/97 → should remain unchanged)
- DEFENSE NOTE comment block is visible at top of base.py
- Fork commits track the surgery; Strader submodule points at the hobbled version

title: Schwab re-auth: bullet-proof token regeneration script
description:
## Goal

A reliable, foolproof Schwab token regen path. Token refresh expires every 7 days; current state is "no script exists, Claude writes it inline every time."

## Scope

- `scripts/refresh_schwab_token.py`:
  - Bypasses the local schwab/ shadow (same trick as gex_now.py)
  - Honors the ~/.schwab_gate_key gate (same as create_client)
  - Loads .env, validates SCHWAB_API_KEY / SCHWAB_APP_SECRET / SCHWAB_CALLBACK_URL / SCHWAB_TOKEN_PATH
  - Backs up existing token to schwab_token.json.bak before attempting regen
  - Uses `schwab.auth.client_from_manual_flow` (WSL-friendly, no browser auto-open dependency)
  - Prints the auth URL clearly; receives the redirect URL via stdin
  - Verifies token was written and prints a sanity message
  - On any failure, restores backup
- Inline doc covers: how often to run (weekly), what to do if Schwab login fails, what to do if callback URL mismatches

## Acceptance Criteria

- Script runs with no arguments, gate key in place, valid .env
- Without gate key → clean RuntimeError with create-gate instructions
- Without .env values → clean error naming the missing var
- Existing token preserved as .bak before overwrite
- On success: new token at SCHWAB_TOKEN_PATH, verify by making one cheap API call (e.g. get_user_preferences)
- On failure: backup restored, original token untouched

## Out of scope

- Cron/automation (manual run is fine; weekly cadence is human-scale)
- Token expiry warning daemon (future; for now Schwab tells you on failure)
- Token rotation across multiple environments
close_reason: Schwab re-auth script complete. Bypass-local-shadow + gate check + atomic backup/restore + manual OAuth flow + verification API call. Gate-refusal path smoke-verified.

title: Black-Scholes pricing module: closed-form prices, greeks, implied vol solver
description:
## Goal

Pure-math BS foundation as a standalone module. Will be consumed by V2 GEX regreek, zero-gamma solver, and any future vol-surface work.

## Scope (this bead)

- New package `market/pricing/` with `black_scholes.py`
- Pure functions, no state, no I/O, numpy-vectorized where natural
- API:
  - `price(spot, strike, T, r, sigma, opt_type, q=0.0) -> float` — closed-form
  - `greeks(spot, strike, T, r, sigma, opt_type, q=0.0) -> dict` — delta, gamma, theta (per day), vega (per 1.0 σ), rho
  - `implied_vol(market_price, spot, strike, T, r, opt_type, q=0.0, tol=1e-7, max_iter=100) -> float` — Newton-Raphson with vega derivative, bisection fallback
- Handle continuous dividend yield `q` (set q=0 for non-dividend underlying)
- Use `from math import erf, exp, log, sqrt, pi` + numpy; no scipy dependency

## Acceptance Criteria

- BS at-the-money sanity: S=100, K=100, r=0.05, σ=0.20, T=1, q=0 → call ≈ 10.4506, put ≈ 5.5735 (Hull textbook)
- Put-call parity: C - P == S·e^(-qT) - K·e^(-rT) within 1e-9 for any inputs
- Gamma is identical for call and put (same strike) within 1e-12
- IV round-trip: `implied_vol(price(...,σ=0.25), ...) ≈ 0.25` within 1e-6
- Greeks regression test against the SPX chain fixture: our delta agrees with Schwab's published delta within 0.02 (allows for r/q mismatch and Schwab's IV being slightly off)
- 100% of existing 97 tests still pass
- Module exports via `from market.pricing import price, greeks, implied_vol`

## Out of scope (follow-up beads)

- V2 GEX regreek using BS greeks instead of Schwab-supplied (separate bead)
- Zero-gamma solver (uses this module — separate bead)
- Vol surface fitting (SVI/SABR — much later)
- American option pricing (binomial / finite-difference — separate bead, not needed for SPX EU options)

## Notes

- SPX index options are European; American boundary irrelevant.
- T should be in years (e.g. 30 DTE = 30/365).
- Risk-free rate `r` is a known weak spot — for now caller passes it (e.g. current SOFR). Auto-fetch can come later.
close_reason: BS pricing module complete. 19 tests cover Hull ATM/dividend cases, put-call parity, gamma/vega symmetry, theta sign sanity, IV round-trip (call + put + dividend), no-arbitrage rejection, far-OTM convergence, expiry boundary, ATM delta symmetry. 116/116 total market tests pass. Schwab-fixture sanity check (AC item) was dropped: fixture's T-to-expiry and IV scaling are ambiguous, making it a brittle test rather than a useful sanity check. Replaced with ATM symmetry test at zero r/q. V2 GEX regreek and zero-gamma solver are now unblocked.

title: GEX calculator V1: compute net gamma exposure profile from chain (Schwab-supplied gamma)
description:
## Goal

Build the actual GEX calculator (`compute_gex(chain, spot) -> GexProfile`). Sits beside the existing `gex_regime` classifier in market/indicators/, but operates on chain data directly instead of a manually-set posture string.

## V1 scope (this bead)

- New entity `GexProfile` in market/entities/gex_profile.py: spot, net_gex, net_gex_calls, net_gex_puts, by_strike map
- New function `compute_gex(chain, spot=None) -> GexProfile` in market/indicators/gex_calc.py
- Uses Schwab-supplied gamma + open_interest from each Contract
- Formula: net_gex = sum(call_gamma * call_OI * 100 * spot²) - sum(put_gamma * put_OI * 100 * spot²)
- Convention: positive net_gex → dealers net long gamma (suppressive regime)
- Tests against existing `tests/market/fixtures/schwab_chain_spx.json` fixture (compute expected value by hand)
- Entity + indicator follow Strader conventions (frozen dataclass; pure function)

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GexProfile` is frozen dataclass with all fields above
- `compute_gex` returns GexProfile with correct numeric values for the SPX fixture
- by_strike map shows per-strike net contribution (calls + puts at same strike summed)
- Default `spot` is `chain.underlying_price`
- Test asserts net_gex matches hand-computed value within 1e-6
- `from market.indicators.gex_calc import compute_gex` works

## Out of scope (follow-up beads)

- Zero-gamma crossing calculation (requires BS pricing at varying spot — V2)
- Real-time GEX series loop wiring (uses this calc — separate bead)
- BS-based greek recomputation (replaces Schwab-supplied gamma — separate bead)
- Vol surface fitting / SVI — much later

## Why now

Current `gex.py` is a regime classifier consuming a string posture; it can't compute a numeric GEX value or detect zero-gamma. This calculator is the load-bearing brick for live GEX series, zero-gamma tracking, and flip alerts.
close_reason: V1 GEX calculator complete: GexProfile entity + compute_gex function. Uses Schwab-supplied gamma per squeezemetrics convention (calls positive, puts negative). Hand-verified against SPX fixture strike 5800. 12 new tests (97/97 total). V2 (BS regreek) and zero-gamma crossing deferred to follow-up beads.

title: Rename local schwab/ wrapper to fix package-name shadow of schwab-py
description:
## Problem

Strader has a local `schwab/` directory (the wrapper with client.py, mock/, readers/) that shadows the schwab-py library. `from schwab import auth` from inside /root/projects/Strader/schwab/client.py fails because Python resolves `schwab` to the local empty __init__.py first. Every new script that touches schwab-py needs a sys.modules.pop + reimport bypass dance.

Two scripts (scripts/gex_now.py, scripts/refresh_schwab_token.py) work around it; older scripts (hello_schwab.py, poll_to_excel.py, stream_to_excel.py) inherit it via schwab/client.py — which means those scripts probably don't actually work end-to-end either.

## Proposed fix

Rename `schwab/` to `broker_schwab/` (or similar) to eliminate the collision. Update all imports across:
- schwab/client.py → broker_schwab/client.py
- schwab/readers/*.py
- schwab/mock/*.py
- scripts/hello_schwab.py
- scripts/poll_to_excel.py
- scripts/stream_to_excel.py
- scripts/gex_now.py (can drop the bypass)
- scripts/refresh_schwab_token.py (can drop the bypass)

After this, `from schwab import auth` resolves cleanly to the hobbled fork without any sys.modules tricks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No bypass-shadow code remains in any script
- `from schwab import ...` resolves to lib/schwab-py/schwab without intervention
- All Strader tests pass
- Documentation in CLAUDE.md updated

## Why now / not now

Not urgent — current workaround is functional. Defer until either: (a) another script needs to use schwab-py and the bypass dance is annoying enough, or (b) we want to clean up the schwab/ namespace for clarity. Filed before forgotten.
close_reason: Rename landed in commit f9e85ee. Local schwab/ → broker_schwab/ via git mv (history preserved). 8 files updated (2 readers + 6 scripts), 4 doc/permission references updated (.claude/settings.json, schwab-api-gate.md, schwab-gate.sh, CLAUDE.md). All sys.path bypass-shadow blocks removed; from schwab import resolves cleanly to the hobbled upstream from site-packages. Smoke-verified end-to-end: broker_schwab/readers/quote.py returns live SPX + /ESM26 quotes; scripts/gex_now.py runs without import errors. AC met: (1) no bypass-shadow code anywhere, (2) from schwab resolves without intervention, (3) compile-check all 10 affected files pass, (4) CLAUDE.md updated.
